decision: Ship agent hiring as a thin HTTP route (POST /api/agents/hire) over a pure hire-service core (src/core/agent-hire.ts), composing four finished pieces atomically: (1) the existing scoped-admin.ts validateAdminDelegation gate authorizes the hire on a {mgmt_object:agent, create, org-scope} grant BEFORE any side-effect; (2) a Keycloak service-account client is created via an INJECTED KeycloakAdminPort (live HTTP adapter in src/keycloak/admin-port.ts, in-memory fake in src/keycloak/fake-admin-port.ts) — Keycloak FIRST so the DB tx is the last mutation and its ROLLBACK is the clean undo; (3) inside one withTenantTx the DAO insertAgentRows (src/db/agent-provision.ts) writes employee(kind='agent') + agent_card (Stage-2 columns NULL, kc_client_id from the port, UNIQUE(tenant_id,kc_client_id) is the conflict guard) and (4) appendAuditEvent writes one agent.hire audit row in the SAME tx. On KC-ok/DB-fail the route best-effort deletes the orphan client. No new migration (042 stays reserved): employee/agent_card/audit schema already exists. The rights layer keys on employee_id only — kc_client_id is never read by grant-resolver/grant-lattice/mcp-tool-registry, so a role-less agent resolves to an empty toolset by construction, not by deny-config.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: A KC failure would require deleting already-committed DB rows against RLS/append-only audit. Keycloak-first makes the DB tx the last mutation (clean ROLLBACK), with a single-client orphan window handled by one best-effort DELETE (NF-4).

rejected_alternatives.option: Call the Keycloak Admin API directly from the route (no port)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Couples the hire core to http + a live Keycloak; unit tests would need a running server (violates NF-7/AC-16). The injected KeycloakAdminPort keeps the core pure and lets the capture-log fake substitute.

rejected_alternatives.option: New migration 042 with a hire_event table
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Redundant with the canonical audit_event chain (FR-6 audits through the same sink as grants). A second event store violates NF-1 and the spec §7 assessment. Slot 042 stays reserved-and-clear (AC-17 vacuous).
Directly violates FR-4 (identity decoupled from rights) and AC-9. The rights layer keys on employee_id; Keycloak identity is invisible by construction.

rejected_alternatives.option: New admin flag/ACL table to authorize the hire
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates NF-1/AC-13. Hire authorization is an ordinary {mgmt_object:agent, create, org-scope} grant checked by the existing validateAdminDelegation — no second authority subsystem.

rejected_alternatives.option: Auto-assign a default agent role on hire
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates FR-5: a freshly hired agent MUST have zero grants (structural least-privilege). Role assignment is a separate admin action (E3.2, out-of-scope).

rejected_alternatives.option: Assign a Keycloak realm role to the service account
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates FR-8/AC-10. Choros rights live in the TS core; the service account carries only actor_type=agent, no realm role.

rejected_alternatives.option: Idempotency via a new idempotency_key column
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Over-builds the best-effort FR-7 NF. The UNIQUE(tenant_id, kc_client_id) constraint is the write-time guard (a retry deriving the same kc_client_id hits the conflict). A dedicated table is deferred.

rejected_alternatives.option: Route the hire under the worker-API / touch JWT validation
rejected_alternatives.why_not: T-0060's seam (E1.4). T-0042 only creates the service account, never validates the agent's token. The hire route is a human-caller admin endpoint under the existing dev-auth seam.
